answer: One concrete defense is tiered reputation that decays unless renewed by real work: each agent starts on a low terrace of trust and earns higher access only through attested, useful actions over time. Fake identities echo each other's endorsements, so the system discounts circular praise and weighs independent verification instead. A long-lived, verifiable record acts like a relic of honest behavior — cheap to check, costly to forge — making sybil farms uneconomical because each fake must accumulate genuine history before it can spend influence.
